civilopediaText.text: The seat of your rule: a Town Hall that grows into a Keep and then a Castle as your realm matures.

name: Monument
uniques: Destroyed when the city is captured

civilopediaText.text: A standing stone carved with the names of the founders. Every town in Azeroth, from Goldshire to Razor Hill, raises one to remember who first held the land.

name: Granary
uniques: [+1 Food] from [Tel'Abim Bananas] tiles [in this city]

civilopediaText.text: Stone storehouses and root cellars that see a town through the long winters of Lordaeron and the dry seasons of the Barrens.
A small wayside shrine: a candle to the Light, a carved totem to the spirits or a bowl of moonwell water, depending on who keeps it.

name: Temple of Elune
uniques: [+15]% Production when constructing [Archery] units [in this city]
[+15]% Production when constructing [Ranged Firearm] units [in this city]

civilopediaText.text: A moonlit temple of the night elves' goddess, whose priestesses have guided their people for ten thousand years.
Quarry yards where masons dress the stone for walls and keeps. The Stonemasons' Guild that rebuilt Stormwind began in yards like these.
A ring of standing stones raised in Arathi by the first humans, where shamans and druids once bound the earth's power.
Shelves of scrolls and tomes, copied by hand. Every great center of learning in Azeroth, Dalaran included, began as a single library.
The heart of Dalaran, city of the Kirin Tor, whose libraries hold the greatest collection of arcane lore in the Eastern Kingdoms.
A ring of packed earth where young warriors test their mettle, as orcs have done since the days of the clans on Draenor.
A wooden wheel on the river grinding grain for the town, the same kind of mill that dotted Elwynn and the Hillsbrad Foothills.

name: Walls
uniques: Destroyed when the city is captured

civilopediaText.text: Timber palisades and stone curtain walls. After the First War no kingdom of men built a city without them.

name: Halls of Origination
uniques: Can build [all] improvements at a [+25]% rate

civilopediaText.text: The titans' vast facility in Uldum, built to shape the world and guarded by the tol'vir since before history began.

name: Uther's Tomb
uniques: Gain [100] [Gold] <upon expending a [Great Person] unit> <(modified by game speed)>

civilopediaText.text: The resting place of Uther the Lightbringer, first of the paladins, slain by his own pupil Arthas in the Plaguelands.

name: Barracks
uniques: New [Military] units start with [15] XP [in this city]
Destroyed when the city is captured

civilopediaText.text: Halls where recruits learn to march, hold a line and follow the horn. In Warcraft's wars every army began in a barracks.
The avenue of statues before the gates of Stormwind, honoring Lothar, Turalyon, Khadgar and the heroes of the Second War.
A beacon tower guiding ships past the reefs, like the lighthouses on the coasts of Westfall and Kul Tiras.
The great lighthouse on the Westfall coast, guiding ships of the Alliance safely past the rocks.

name: Stable
uniques: [+15]% Production when constructing [Mounted] units [in this city]

civilopediaText.text: Paddocks and stalls for the mounts of the realm: horses, wolves, rams, kodos or striders, each race to its own.

name: Grand Coliseum
uniques: Only available <if [Arena] is constructed in all [non-[Puppeted]] cities>
Cost increases by [30] per owned city

civilopediaText.text: An arena in the manner of the Ring of Valor and the Gurubashi Arena, where champions fight for glory and gold.

name: Magistrate's Hall
uniques: Removes extra unhappiness from annexed cities

civilopediaText.text: Where a magistrate hears disputes and collects the crown's due, keeping the outlying towns loyal to the capital.
The sacred heart of Pandaria, where the waters of the Pools of Power once nourished an eternal spring.
A stone arena where champions fight before cheering crowds, much like the Ring of Valor in Orgrimmar or the Gurubashi Arena.
The mogu emperors' vaults beneath Kun-Lai, where an army of stone guardians waits to be woken.

name: Temple
uniques: Destroyed when the city is captured

civilopediaText.text: A house of worship and healing, the heart of faith in any city: a cathedral nave, a moon temple or a hall of the ancestors.

name: Grand Library
uniques: Only available <if [Library] is constructed in all [non-[Puppeted]] cities>
Cost increases by [30] per owned city

civilopediaText.text: A great library on the model of the Royal Library of Stormwind, where scribes copy every tome they can find.
Where the oracles of Sholazar and the seers of the Exodar read the threads of fate.

name: Amphitheater
uniques: Destroyed when the city is captured

civilopediaText.text: Tiered stone seats around a stage where bards and players tell the old stories of the Troll Wars and the founding of the kingdoms.

name: Hall of Legends
uniques: Only available <if [Monument] is constructed in all [non-[Puppeted]] cities>
Cost increases by [30] per owned city

civilopediaText.text: A hall where bards and lorewalkers keep the songs and sagas of your people.
A square of stalls and carts where farmers, hunters and traveling goblins trade their goods.

name: Mint
uniques: [+2 Gold] from [Gold Ore] tiles [in this city]

civilopediaText.text: Where gold and silver ore become coin stamped with the realm's seal. Every kingdom trusts its own coin, and every goblin trusts all of them.

name: Caverns of Time
uniques: [+1 Food, +1 Production, +1 Gold] from [Desert] tiles without [Flood plains] [in this city]

civilopediaText.text: The lair of the bronze dragonflight in Tanaris, where Nozdormu's servants guard the true timeline.

name: Aqueduct
uniques: [40]% Food is carried over after population increases [in this city]

civilopediaText.text: Stone channels carrying fresh water into the city, so that it can grow beyond the reach of its wells.

name: The Greymane Wall
uniques: Enemy [Land] units must spend [1] extra movement points when inside your territory <before discovering [Seaforium]> <Suppress warning [*contains a conditional on a unit movement unique*]>

civilopediaText.text: The great wall Genn Greymane raised to cut Gilneas off from the troubles of the other kingdoms.

name: Hall of Champions
uniques: Only available <if [Barracks] is constructed in all [non-[Puppeted]] cities>
All newly-trained [non-[Air]] units [in this city] receive the [Morale] promotion
Cost increases by [30] per owned city

civilopediaText.text: Where your greatest warriors are honored, and from which new recruits march with their courage high.
The great harbor of Kul Tiras and its admiralty, home of the Proudmoore fleets.
Walled gardens of herbs and flowers, tended for beauty and for the apothecary's shelves.
The great cathedral of Stormwind, seat of the Church of the Holy Light and its archbishops.

name: Shrine of Seven Stars
uniques: All newly-trained [Missionary] units [in this city] receive the [Devout] promotion
All newly-trained [Great Prophet] units [in this city] receive the [Devout] promotion

civilopediaText.text: The Alliance's embassy in the Vale of Eternal Blossoms, a place of scholarship and trade.

name: High Temple
uniques: Only available <if [Temple] is constructed in all [non-[Puppeted]] cities>
Cost increases by [30] per owned city

civilopediaText.text: The holy seat of your people's faith, where its highest priests gather.
The great jungle city of the Gurubashi trolls in Stranglethorn, once given over to the blood god Hakkar.

name: Royal Vault
uniques: Only available <if [Market] is constructed in all [non-[Puppeted]] cities>
Cost increases by [30] per owned city

civilopediaText.text: The guarded treasury of the realm, behind doors no thief has ever opened.

name: Thunder Totem
uniques: Must have an owned [{non-[Natural Wonder]} {Mountain}] within [2] tiles

civilopediaText.text: The towering totem of the Highmountain tauren, carved with the story of every tribe.
Workbenches, forges and gear-cutting lathes, where tinkers and smiths turn out the tools a city needs.

name: Blacksmith
uniques: [+15]% Production when constructing [Land] units [in this city]

civilopediaText.text: The forge and anvil where weapons and armor are made and mended. In Warcraft III a Blacksmith's upgrades kept an army in the fight.

name: Shipyard
uniques: [+1 Production] from [Water resource] tiles [in this city]

civilopediaText.text: Slipways and timber yards where hulls are laid down, like the great shipyards of Boralus.
A sanctum where mages study and practice their craft. In Warcraft III, Arcane Sanctums trained the Alliance's priests and sorceresses.

name: College of Magi
uniques: Only available <if [Arcane Sanctum] is constructed in all [non-[Puppeted]] cities>
Cost increases by [30] per owned city

civilopediaText.text: An academy of the arcane on the model of Dalaran's, where young mages learn to master their power.

name: Temple of the White Tiger
uniques: [-25]% Culture cost of natural border growth [in all cities]
[-25]% Gold cost of acquiring tiles [in all cities]

civilopediaText.text: The temple of Xuen, the celestial White Tiger, high in Kun-Lai Summit, where pandaren train body and spirit.

name: Keep
uniques: Destroyed when the city is captured

civilopediaText.text: A fortified stone keep at the heart of the city, the second stage of a Warcraft town hall.

name: Sunfury Spire
uniques: All newly-trained [relevant] units [in this city] receive the [Weapon Mastery I] promotion

civilopediaText.text: The palace of the Sunstrider dynasty in Silvermoon, its red-and-gold halls glowing with arcane light.

name: Great Foundry
uniques: Only available <if [Workshop] is constructed in all [non-[Puppeted]] cities>
Cost increases by [30] per owned city

civilopediaText.text: A foundry in the spirit of Ironforge's Great Forge, whose fires never go out.
The abbey in Elwynn Forest where the brothers of the Light train every young priest and paladin of Stormwind.

name: Armory
uniques: New [Military] units start with [15] XP [in this city]
Destroyed when the city is captured

civilopediaText.text: Racks of spears, shields and mail, kept ready so a city can arm its levies at a moment's notice.
A domed tower for watching the stars and the twin moons, much as the Titans' watchers once charted Azeroth's skies.

name: Bardic Hall
uniques: Destroyed when the city is captured

civilopediaText.text: A hall of music and song, where bards keep alive the ballads of heroes and the laments of fallen kingdoms.
Medivh's tower in Deadwind Pass, built on a nexus of ley lines and full of strange echoes of the past.
Vaults and counting tables. The banks of Stormwind, Ironforge and Orgrimmar hold a city's wealth, and its secrets.
The constables and guards who keep the peace in the streets, like the Stormwind City Guard and Orgrimmar's Grunts.
The palace of the mogu emperors in the Vale, later home of the Golden Lotus.
Pens and cages for the great beasts a city tames: gryphons, wyverns, hippogryphs and stranger things.
The tower of the mage Theocritus in Elwynn Forest, its leaning silhouette visible for miles.

name: Grim Batol
uniques: [+15]% Strength <for [All] units> <when fighting in [Friendly Land] tiles>

civilopediaText.text: The great fortress of the Wildhammer dwarves in the Wetlands, cursed and abandoned, later a stronghold of the Dragonmaw.

name: Port
uniques: [+1 Production, +1 Gold] from [Water resource] tiles [in this city]
[+15]% Production when constructing [Water] units [in this city]

civilopediaText.text: Docks, warehouses and a harbormaster's office: the gateway for a city's trade across the Great Sea.

name: Royal Gallery
uniques: Only available <if [Bardic Hall] is constructed in all [non-[Puppeted]] cities>
Cost increases by [30] per owned city

civilopediaText.text: A gallery of treasures, paintings and trophies gathered from every corner of Azeroth.
The Sunwell of Quel'Danas, the fount of holy and arcane power that sustains the elves of Quel'Thalas.
The titan city in the Storm Peaks, prison of the Old God Yogg-Saron and seat of the Keepers.

name: Windmill
uniques: [+10]% Production when constructing [All] buildings [in this city]

civilopediaText.text: Sails turning on the hill to grind the harvest; the windmills of Westfall are known across the Eastern Kingdoms.

name: Arsenal
uniques: Destroyed when the city is captured

civilopediaText.text: A great storehouse of powder, shot and siege engines, kept for the wars to come.
The Lich King's fortress atop the Frozen Throne, rising from the glacier of Icecrown.

name: Museum
uniques: Destroyed when the city is captured

civilopediaText.text: Halls of relics and curiosities, much like the Explorers' League collections in Ironforge's Hall of Explorers.
The museum of the Explorers' League in Ironforge, home of Brann Bronzebeard's discoveries.
A tall tower of the Kirin Tor style, its upper floors given over to spellcraft and its library to forbidden tomes.
Roaring furnaces and steam-driven hammers turning out iron by the ton, like the Great Forge of Ironforge.

name: Undermine Exchange
uniques: [Gold] cost of purchasing items in cities [-15]%

civilopediaText.text: The trade hub of the goblin cartels beneath Kezan, where fortunes are made and lost in an hour.

name: Training Grounds
uniques: New [Military] units start with [15] XP [in this city]
Destroyed when the city is captured

civilopediaText.text: Fields for drilling troops in formation, archery butts and practice dummies scarred by a thousand recruits.

name: Gates of Ahn'Qiraj
uniques: New [Military] units start with [15] XP [in this city]

civilopediaText.text: The Scarab Wall in Silithus, sealing the qiraji and their Old God master away from the world.
A hospice run by priests and herbalists, where the sick and wounded are tended with prayer and poultice.
Where everything has a price. The goblins of the Steamwheedle Cartel run the auction houses of Azeroth, and take their cut.
Water-wheels and tide-mills turning the sea's motion into power, a gnomish and Kul Tiran craft.
A stone tower with a watch fire on top, one of a chain that sends warnings across the realm.
A great arena of the late ages, hosting tournaments to rival the Argent Tournament in Icecrown.

name: Arcane Beacon
uniques: Destroyed when the city is captured

civilopediaText.text: A crystal spire that sends the city's news and orders across the realm by arcane signal.
The great temple of the dragonflights in Dragonblight, where the Aspects meet.

name: Spymaster's Guild
uniques: Only available <if [Guard Tower] is constructed in all [non-[Puppeted]] cities>
Cost increases by [30] per owned city

civilopediaText.text: A network of spies and agents on the model of SI:7, the shadows that protect the realm.

name: Fortress
uniques: Destroyed when the city is captured

civilopediaText.text: A citadel of stone and iron, the last refuge of a city under siege, the third stage of a Warcraft town hall.

name: Lion's Rest
uniques: [+1 Production] from every specialist [in all cities]

civilopediaText.text: The monument at Stormwind's gate to the heroes who fell at the Wrathgate in Northrend.

name: Shadowfang Keep
uniques: Must have an owned [{non-[Natural Wonder]} {Mountain}] within [2] tiles

civilopediaText.text: Archmage Arugal's castle above Pyrewood, overrun by his worgen.
Workrooms of enchanted glassware and humming crystals, where arcanists push the boundaries of their art.

name: Seat of the Naaru
uniques: [-10]% Culture cost of adopting new Policies

civilopediaText.text: Where the naaru, beings of pure Light, speak with the faithful, as in the Exodar and Shattrath.

name: Alchemy Lab
uniques: [25]% Food is carried over after population increases [in this city]

civilopediaText.text: Bubbling flasks and reeking vapors: potions, elixirs and the occasional explosion.

name: Mana Bomb Project
uniques: Triggers a global alert upon completion

civilopediaText.text: The arcane foundries where the terrible mana bombs are made, like the one that destroyed Theramore.
The great hall of the Warchief in Orgrimmar, named for Grom Hellscream.

name: Sun Crystal Array
uniques: Only available <in cities without a [Mana Reactor]>

civilopediaText.text: Rows of sun-catching crystals that gather light and turn it into arcane power, in the style of Silvermoon.
Mountains of scrap, sorted by goblin crews who can build something useful from anything.
The palace of the nightborne elves in Suramar City, built around the Nightwell.

name: Mana Reactor
uniques: Only available <in cities without a [Sun Crystal Array]>

civilopediaText.text: A contained well of arcane energy feeding a whole city's engines. Dangerous, and very efficient.

name: Titan Ascension Project
uniques: Triggers a global alert upon completion

civilopediaText.text: Once you have completed the Titan Ascension Project, you can start constructing Titan vessel parts in your cities (with the relevant technologies) to win a Scientific Victory!
A shield of arcane wards over the realm, like the dome that protected Quel'Thalas.

name: Mechagon Spire
uniques: Gain a free [Arcane Beacon] [in all cities]

civilopediaText.text: The spire of Mechagon, the mechagnomes' island of gears and steam.

name: Burrow
uniques: Population loss from nuclear attacks [-75]% [in this city]
Damage to garrison from nuclear attacks [-75]% [in this city]
Only available <when nuclear weapons are enabled> <hidden from users>

civilopediaText.text: Fortified burrows and shelters dug deep beneath the city, like the orc burrows of Warcraft II.

name: Celestial Planetarium
uniques: [+25]% Production when constructing [Spaceship part] units [in this city]
Gain a free [Skyship Foundry] [in this city]

civilopediaText.text: An observatory of the titans' design that charts the stars and the worlds beyond them.

name: Skyship Foundry
uniques: [+50]% Production when constructing [Spaceship part] units [in this city]

civilopediaText.text: Slipways for airships, with gas envelopes inflating overhead, building the fleets that rule the skies of the late ages.

name: Grand Council of Azeroth
uniques: Triggers voting for the Diplomatic Victory
Triggers a global alert upon completion

civilopediaText.text: A council of all the peoples of Azeroth, gathered to face the threats no one race can face alone.

name: Well of Eternity
uniques: Unavailable <when number of [Completed Policy branches] is less than [5]>
Triggers a global alert upon build start
Triggers a Cultural Victory upon completion

civilopediaText.text: The restoration of the Well of Eternity, the source of all magic in the ancient world.
A soaring cathedral of the Light, its windows of stained glass, its bells calling the faithful to prayer.

name: Monastery
uniques: [+1 Culture, +1 Faith] from [Ale] tiles [in this city]
[+1 Culture, +1 Faith] from [Mageroyal] tiles [in this city]
Destroyed when the city is captured

civilopediaText.text: A quiet cloister of monks and scholars, like the Scarlet Monastery in its better days or the monasteries of Pandaria.
A sacred sanctuary where pilgrims rest and seek the wisdom of their faith.
A tiered pagoda in the Pandaren manner, where incense rises and the faithful meditate.

name: Chapel of the Light
uniques: Destroyed when the city is captured

civilopediaText.text: Bells ring out from these chapels in every human town, calling the faithful to the Holy Light. Provides more Faith and Culture than the Temple it replaces.

name: Royal Barracks
uniques: New [Military] units start with [25] XP [in this city]
Destroyed when the city is captured

civilopediaText.text: Where the footmen and knights of the human kingdoms drill until the shield-wall moves as one. New military units start with 25 experience instead of 15.
Human towns grow from the forests of Elwynn and the fields of Westfall. The Lumber Mill gives more Production than a Workshop and +1 Production from Forests worked by the city.

name: Castle
uniques: Destroyed when the city is captured

civilopediaText.text: Town Hall, Keep, Castle: every human city of note rises in stone. Stronger defenses than the Keep it replaces, and +1 Culture.

name: Altar of Kings
uniques: Cost increases by [30] per owned city

civilopediaText.text: Where the heroes of the human kingdoms are honored and new champions are called to lead. A free Great General appears when it is built; +15% Great Person generation in this city. Only the Humans can build it, once.
